For sequence i with mᵢ supervised targets and target gradients gᵢⱼ, pooled per-target averaging gives Gₜ=Σᵢⱼgᵢⱼ/Σᵢmᵢ; averaging within each sequence first gives Gₛ=(1/B)Σᵢ[Σⱼgᵢⱼ/mᵢ]. Algebraically, the former weights sequences by target count; the latter weights sequences equally. They coincide when counts are equal. Summing targets then averaging sequences additionally scales gradients with supervision count. With random counts, expected gradients retain these sampling-dependent weights; an expected ratio cannot generally become a ratio of expectations. Thus nominal terminal/reconstruction coefficients do not establish equal target exposure or gradient influence. Report branch sampling probabilities, reductions, denominators and target-count distributions. PyTorch’s unweighted cross-entropy mean excludes ignored targets. [Loss documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html)

Recommended paired audit: evaluate both objectives at identical frozen parameters on matched histories; record corruption masks, supervised positions, candidate sampling, seeds, checkpoint, precision and software versions. Disable dropout while retaining autograd, or replay matched dropout randomness and explicitly report that protocol. Preserve RNG/model state and perform no optimizer steps, clipping or adaptive reweighting. Compare raw gradients and coefficient-scaled gradients separately; include a target-count-matched control because changing reduction cannot remove differences in context, target positions or exposure. [Autograd modes](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd)

Define disjoint parameter blocks and fixed flattening order; count tied embeddings once, including their combined input/output gradient. Use autograd.grad to avoid accumulation; retain unused-parameter flags while representing missing gradients as zeros. Report both block norms, norm ratios and cosine, specifying thresholds; zero-norm cosine is undefined, so report its frequency separately. Aggregate paired measurements across batches with uncertainty, distinguishing mean batch cosine from cosine of mean gradients. [Parameter deduplication](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html), [gradient API](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad.html)
